chapter: Charley Johnson and the Army band
title: Army band repertoire and French audiences
summary: He confirms the Bugle Blues is the Bugle Call Rag, says the band played ragtime and marches, and played for French townspeople.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Getting back to the music, the 'Bugle Blues' that you mentioned before is, of course, the same as the 'Bugle Call Rag', right?
Yeah.
The same tune.
The 'Bugle Call Rag'.
Right, which Benny Goodman did and a
Many of our dancers used to dance to that.
Right.
You see, so that's how that happened.
But, but the music you played, that your band played in the Army, did you play for dances, for instance?
Oh, yeah, but they didn't play nothing. (Habernola), and some other pieces. And I didn't play much with that.
But there was no jazz involved in that?

No, no, there wasn't no jazz. Cause they didn't have any jazz, then. Not those boys. They were -- we had some of them there, and some of them are still living around here. But what they had, they called Ragtime.
Yeah, so did you play Ragtime melodies with that band?
Yeah, we played some. We used to swing up, jazz up, over there and keep the home fires burning, and things like that, but it was nothing of what we call jazz today, you know?
I see. But, did Europeans hear you too?
Oh, yes.
So, what you did with the Ragtime
melodies must have been something new to them.

Yes, it was new to them. Because we had to play guard mount every evening, see? And so, when we played guard mount, and retreat, and after the retreat, they'd close it up, and the boys would stay there and play a couple.

In Barcelaubc, one place there in France, we were stationed there for about four or five months. Well, we used to play there and the French youngsters used to come out and the old people enjoyed it, too. We'd give them two or three numbers and then we'd march on back.
